requirement.original: 提供修复丢失的codex session的方案
requirement.clarified: Produce an actionable recovery plan for codex session 019dd077-6d3c-7de1-bd6d-145b8ee35a45 (cgroup-killed by unauthorized happy-daemon-dev restart at 2026-05-04 22:16:00). Plan must restore user access via dev UI sidebar with conversation history intact, exclude 5 subagent threads from user-facing surfacing, and use only user-run TTY commands plus dev-UI Playwright verification — no daemon HTTP/API/curl session creation, no daemon restarts, no code changes.
requirement.what: Recovery plan exercising the existing /root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh `recover <uuid>` subcommand to spawn a new codex session that resumes thread-id 019dd077 against happy-daemon-dev, plus a Playwright verification SOP on dev.life-ai.app.
requirement.why: User lost a 7-day-running codex conversation when an unauthorized daemon restart killed the cgroup. The rollout JSONL is preserved on disk (2.45MB). The watcher's auto-restore path requires a live process holding an fd to the rollout, which does not exist post-kill — manual `recover` is needed. User-sim explicitly clarified the mental model: 'open dev UI, see session in sidebar, click, pick up conversation.'

current_state_diagnostic.summary: PATH C — watcher hasn't auto-restored 019dd077 because its scan_codex_via_fd source requires a LIVE process fd, and the codex CLI process is dead. Rollout file is preserved. Manual recovery via the watcher script's `recover <uuid>` subcommand is required.

path_a_watcher_already_restored.evidence: pgrep -af '019dd077-6d3c-7de1-bd6d-145b8ee35a45' returns zero non-grep matches; /root/.happy-dev/session_dirs.txt mtime 22:27 (post-restart) does not contain 019dd077 nor any codex tid; daemon log /root/.happy-dev/logs/2026-05-04-22-16-02-pid-1596472-daemon.log shows zero spawn events for 019dd077.

path_b_watcher_tried_and_failed.evidence: Daemon log shows zero spawn attempts for 019dd077 since the 22:16 restart; no error to investigate.

path_c_watcher_hasnt_run_or_doesnt_suppo.evidence: scan_codex_via_fd (happy-session-recovery.sh:798-818) requires the codex process to hold an open fd to the rollout JSONL — with the cgroup-killed process gone, the fd is closed, so the tid never enters the watcher's enumeration. The script DOES support codex tids in the manual `recover <uuid>` path (auto-detects via is_codex_thread_id at line 1163; finds rollout via find_codex_rollout at 1241; spawns via daemon_spawn_session with flavor=codex passing --resume <tid> at line 873-874). The 22:10 snapshot pre-kill confirmed the script CAN see codex tids when their process is alive — the only gap is post-death recovery, which requires the manual subcommand.

path_d_other.evidence: No other recovery vector in scope; codex CLI's own `codex resume <tid>` outside happy-cli wrapper is a fallback only mentioned in failure-mode B.

recovery_path.chosen: User-run `bash /root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh recover 019dd077-6d3c-7de1-bd6d-145b8ee35a45 --home /root/.happy-dev` from TTY, followed by Playwright UI verification on https://dev.life-ai.app at desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844.
recovery_path.rationale: Existing sanctioned tooling. No code changes. No daemon restart. Smallest, safest, most deterministic path that exercises the codex resume protocol the way it was designed. Aligned with user binding directive ('实现方式是最小最安全最完美最确定性地实现用户的需求，而不是扩大修复范围').

alternatives_considered.reason: scan_codex_via_fd needs a live process fd; with the cgroup kill, no fd exists. Watcher can't see 019dd077 unless it's already running.

alternatives_considered.name: Subagent runs the recovery script
alternatives_considered.reason: happy-session-recovery.sh is permanently hook-blocked for subagents per /root/.claude/hooks/pretool-bash-safety.sh — and per CLAUDE.md, only the user runs it manually from TTY.

alternatives_considered.name: Subagent calls daemon HTTP /spawn-session or server /v1/sessions
alternatives_considered.reason: FORBIDDEN by CLAUDE.md ('NEVER use code/API/curl to create sessions'). Hook-blocked. Would also bypass the per-tid spawn lock that prevents double-spawn races.

alternatives_considered.name: Restart happy-daemon-dev and let it auto-restore on startup
alternatives_considered.reason: Daemon is healthy. Restarting would kill ANY active codex session in the cgroup — which is exactly the catastrophe that produced this incident. Furthermore, the daemon's startup auto-restore reads session_dirs.txt — which doesn't contain 019dd077 — so a restart would NOT restore it.

alternatives_considered.name: Codex CLI's own `codex resume <tid>` outside happy-cli wrapper
alternatives_considered.reason: If the happy-cli wrapper's resume creates a fresh thread on the codex backend (failure-mode B), the user can still inspect/use the rollout via codex CLI directly. Not the primary path because it bypasses happy-cli/happy-server integration — the new conversation wouldn't appear in the dev UI sidebar.

root_cause_analysis.symptom: Codex session 019dd077 lost from dev UI sidebar; user can no longer access the 7-day-running conversation through the standard UI flow.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: Unauthorized happy-daemon-dev restart at 2026-05-04 22:16:00 cgroup-killed the codex CLI child process holding tid 019dd077. The watcher's auto-enumeration path (scan_codex_via_fd) requires a live process fd, so post-kill the tid is dropped from session_dirs.txt and snapshots — leaving the rollout JSONL preserved on disk but invisible to the auto-restore loop.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A — incident, not commit-traceable. The unauthorized restart was the immediate cause; the deeper structural cause is daemon→child cgroup coupling (the daemon's systemd cgroup contains its spawned codex CLI processes, so daemon restart kills children). Sibling architect spec architect-happy-restart-and-daemon-prohibition-20260504-223115.md addresses prevention.
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: happy-cli's daemon model spawns codex via Node.js child_process, inheriting the daemon's cgroup membership. This is the standard systemd unit topology — not a bug.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: Restarts of the daemon (intentional or accidental) terminate ALL active codex/claude sessions under that daemon, even though the daemon itself does not 'own' the sessions in any logical sense. Recovery exists for this case (the watcher script and codex's rollout-on-disk model), but the recovery is opt-in and requires either a live fd (auto-path) or manual `recover` (TTY-path).
root_cause_analysis.timeline: 2026-04-27 19:43 — codex thread 019dd077 created. 2026-04-27 22:16 — last activity (rollout mtime). 2026-04-27 to 2026-05-04 — thread dormant but happy-cli process held the fd (heartbeats kept alive). 2026-05-04 22:16:00 — unauthorized happy-daemon-dev restart, cgroup kill, fd lost. 2026-05-04 22:27 — first post-restart watcher snapshot omits 019dd077.

pre_existing_guards.purpose: Per-tid spawn lock — prevents two simultaneous spawns of the same tid (auto-restore + manual recover collision per codex risk #5).
